contract.scientific_mechanism: A more realistic spatial current distribution in an extended but dipole-dominated radiator modifies the far-zone dipole form factor, changing how directional emission is progressively suppressed as wavelength approaches source size.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient correction because the changed denominator introduces a bounded saturation in the joint omega-theta suppression coordinate, altering angular-profile curvature across frequencies rather than merely rescaling amplitude or shifting one onset parameter.
contract.assumption_before: The source-size correction can be represented by the current single exponential function of omega/omega_size and sin(theta)^2.
contract.assumption_after: The finite-size correction follows a smoother extended-source dipole form factor whose angular contribution saturates with the combined size-direction coordinate.
contract.parent_reduction: In the weak finite-size limit omega/omega_size << 1, the added ((omega/omega_size)**2)*sin(theta)**2 term is higher order, so the child reduces to the parent to leading order and both approach the point-dipole law.
contract.observable_signature: Compare S_rad(theta) at fixed p_0 and r for one frequency with omega/omega_size << 1 and another with omega/omega_size ~ 1. The parent predicts a single locked-curvature angular suppression family, whereas the child shows a saturating reshaping: intermediate-angle attenuation grows differently from near-equatorial attenuation, changing the lobe curvature without moving the axial zeros or the overall r^-2 decay.
contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting the parent's single omega_size can only globally stretch the original exponential's frequency-angle dependence, leaving its curvature relation between intermediate and near-equatorial angles fixed. Across the admissible pair of low and order-unity omega/omega_size conditions, one shared parent parameter set cannot reproduce the child's frequency-dependent saturation of the angular suppression because the target mapping S_rad(omega, theta) itself changes shape, not just scale.
